Welcome to my personal website. I am a Lecturer (Teaching and Leadership) at Macquarie University, passionate about teaching and learning in statistics or anything that can use statistics.
Browse my Teaching page to learn more about my units and teaching philosophy.

title: About
text:
I am a Lecturer (Teaching and Leadership) in the School of Mathematical and Physical Sciences at Macquarie University, with a 70% teaching and 30% leadership role.
My research interests include variable selection, stability selection, complex modelling, and statistical graphics.

title: Teaching
text:
A core concept that is taught to first year undergraduate students is the concepts of a population and a sample. We also tackle the idea that all samples should be representative of the target population. As I spend more time in Higher Education and teach a wider array of students, I am starting to wonder, will any sample of students ever be representative of a cohort? More importantly, does it need to be? I don’t think it does. The diversity in every classroom is not a problem to control for - it’s the very thing that makes teaching worthwhile.
To simplify my approach to teaching, the key steps are:

Break down barriers and enable conversation,
Promote and reward curiosity,
Support those who want to learn, and
Remember everyone is different and there are many different ways to learn.

Let \(X\) be a continuous random variable where all raw moments exist. Just because we might know \(\mathbb{E}(X)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(X)\) does not mean we can extrapolate information about anything higher order. (We see grades and attendance patterns, but that is only part of the story.)
